brief.headline: Push for ₹290/KG (the price Shrinath gives us) to save ₹3.91 L/yr, and line up a second source — they lost ₹-23.68 Cr last year and carry five risk flags, so steady supply is at risk.

priceAsk.summary: Ask them to match ₹290/KG, the price Shrinath Roto Pack already gives us for the same laminates.
priceAsk.basis: We pay them ₹295/KG but Shrinath charges ₹290/KG for identical material (LM ELECTRAL sachets). The market asking price for pharma ORS laminate sits at ₹205–305/kg (typical ₹250/kg), so our ₹295 is at the top of the fair band — there's room to come down to ₹290 and still be market-fair.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Keep the current 30 Days After Receipt — do not offer faster payment.

brief.financialLeverage: GLS lost ₹-23.68 Cr in FY2024-25 and carries five red flags: loss-making, severe legal cases, GST filing delays, EPF payment delays, and high debt (2.15x). Their money-health score is 2/10, and the Altman Z-score of 1.68 puts them in the grey zone (heightened risk of trouble). We are 0.33% of their ₹691.05 Cr revenue — tiny — so losing us won't tip them over, but their fragility means a hard price squeeze could hurt supply. Lead with the ₹290 benchmark (which is fair) and a promise of steady volume, not aggressive payment cuts. Most important: qualify Huhtamaki or UFLEX as a live second source so we're not stuck if GLS stumbles.

evidence.figure: Loss-making (FY2024-25), Severe legal case(s), GST filing delays, EPF payment delays, High leverage (2.1x)

evidence.point: Altman Z-score shows heightened distress risk
We are a tiny slice of their business
We pay ₹5/KG more than our cheapest supplier on key SKUs
evidence.figure: ₹295/KG vs ₹290/KG (Shrinath Roto Pack); gap 1.7%, costing ₹3.91 L/yr

alternates.name: Huhtamaki India Ltd
alternates.why: Listed flexible-packaging converter, already a small FDC supplier — a proven, scalable second source for laminate sachets (a lead to qualify: verify capacity and price before RFQ).

alternates.name: UFLEX Ltd
alternates.why: Listed flexibles giant that makes both film and does conversion — can second-source laminates at scale (a lead to qualify: verify before RFQ).

alternates.name: Constantia Parikh Packaging Pvt Ltd
alternates.why: Part of the global Constantia group, focused on pharma blister and sachet laminates; health score D (31/100), revenue ₹222.04 Cr — a strong second-source candidate (a lead to qualify: verify before RFQ).

risks: They lost ₹-23.68 Cr last year and sit in the grey distress zone (1.68 Altman Z) — pushing too hard on price could break supply; keep the ask modest and line up a backup fast.
Five red flags (loss-making, legal cases, GST delays, EPF delays, 2.15x debt) mean continuity risk is real — do not increase share-of-wallet until a second source is live.
Their credit rating is IVR BBB- / Stable (middling) and money-health is 2/10 — watch payment behaviour and delivery closely; any slip is an early-warning sign.
We are only 0.33% of their revenue, so they may not prioritise us in a crunch — having Huhtamaki or UFLEX qualified gives us leverage and a safety net.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We value the partnership, but we're paying ₹295 when Shrinath gives us ₹290 for the same laminate — let's close that ₹5 gap and talk about how we keep volume steady for you.
